correctness.rationale: With R=1+B_a, scale theta=epsilon*t. The limit 2/(1-it) and the bound by C/(1+|t|) give the displayed gamma constant by integration. The identity R times conjugate(B_a)=conjugate(R), evenness under conjugation, and Re R=|R|²/2 give the exact total mass of the linear variation. Its absolute density is bounded by |R|^(p-1), with mass O(epsilon) and o(epsilon) outside each fixed arc of 1; this gives the indicated evaluation functional uniformly on bounded polynomial sets. Uniform convexity bounds the unscaled perturbation by O(delta). On the delta scale, Taylor remainders divided by delta^p are bounded by constants times delta^(2-p) integral|R|^(p-2) and delta^(-1) integral|R|. The first tends to zero: for 2<p<3 use (epsilon/delta)^(p-2), at p=3 use delta log(1/epsilon), and for p>3 use delta. The second is O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)/delta). This proves bounded-set convergence of the normalized objectives and hence convergence of minimizers and minima by strict convexity and compactness in fixed degree, including n=0. Conjugation and reversal give equal real coefficients in degree one; optimizing its scalar objective gives c_p and the stated decrement. Point evaluation and its explicit extremizer give the exact unrestricted optimum; the log derivative of C_0 vanishes at 2 and is strictly positive thereafter by strict decrease of trigamma. The even-power baseline follows by the inner function mean-value identity and the already verified linear coefficient. As a check on the supplied quartic code, direct expansion with g=B_a(u+vz) gives integral|1-g|⁴=1+4 integral|g|²+integral|g|⁴−4 Re integral(g+g|g|²)+2 Re integral g². Here integral(g|g|²)=−a(u³+2uv²)+(1−a²)u²v for real u,v, confirming the quartic formula and its baseline 6−8a+2a².
residual_risks: The theorem fixes p>2 and n before the limit; the estimates do not justify uniformity as p→2 or n→infinity.

The exact-baseline formulation is correct, but the suggestion that a non-even p requires it to avoid intervening powers at the displayed order is unnecessary. Push forward circle measure by B_a to the Poisson kernel of −a, so with r=|1+w| the baseline is (1−a²) times integral r^p/(epsilon²+a r²). Subtracting (1−a²)/a times integral r^(p−2) leaves O(epsilon^p) for 2<p<3, O(epsilon³ log(1/epsilon)) at p=3, and O(epsilon³) for p>3. The baseline therefore is C_0(p)epsilon+O(epsilon²) throughout p>2. This strengthens rather than contradicts the Finding; the caution in the limitations should not be read as claiming an intervening power before the displayed correction.

value.rationale: Continuity alone hides how strongly a fixed polynomial degree constrains approximation as the Blaschke zero approaches the boundary. The theorem identifies the singular response and a nonvanishing relative gap from the exact unrestricted optimum for every fixed degree, then makes the first polynomial correction quantitative. That is a substantive asymptotic obstruction in a standard extremal problem, not a recomputation of an analytic distance.
residual_risks: No uniform cutoff for a growing degree, or joint p and a limit, is supplied.
